candidate.name: sc_s3c_mbs
candidate.label: (s3c-mbs)
candidate.definition: (s3c) with indicator terms added to (s3)'s fit: one 0/1 indicator per class, mbs_a to mbs_d, 1 on a target day that is a settlement day of that class when the day's year was public at the decision instant (else 0). If a class has fewer than 20 settlement days in the window, the four classes pool into one indicator, mbs_any, that is 1 on a settlement day of any class. Every other term, the Huber fit, the ridge of 5 and the SRF cap at full allotment (margin 0 bp, repo_model.s3c_candidate) are (s3c)'s and are not changed
candidate.module: repo_model.s3c_mbs (MbsTable, class_counts, must_pool, fit_mbs_terms, forecast_leads, walk) and repo_model.sifma_mbs (the source); the cap, the line and the full-allotment flag are repo_model.s3c_candidate's and repo_model.srf_line's, unchanged
candidate.window_for_pooling: the development window: the panel's rows with date up to 2025-12-31, each counted once per class when its indicator, read at lead 1 (the decision the row before), is 1; the settlement days of a year that was not public are not counted. A class below 20 pools all four. The counts and the outcome are in result.json and on the page, and the study states which it used
candidate.units: the indicators are 0/1 columns like the other flag terms of (s3), in standardised units: the target is raw / scale(origin), the coefficient is the effect in scale units, and the effect in bp is the coefficient times the scale at the decision's anchor. A forecast adds scale(anchor) * sum(coefficient_k * indicator_k) to every quantile
candidate.entry: an indicator enters a lead's fit when at least 3 training pairs (MIN_FLAGGED, as for the flag terms) carry it; the intercept is dropped, so the pool keeps the ordinary-day centre. Where none enters, the estimate is spread_mr_state_calendar.fit_state_terms' on the same pairs, element for element
candidate.information_set: a new availability rule, in metadata/sifma_mbs_1276.json. The indicator of target row r read at lead h is that of the date of r under the rule at the decision instant of row r - h (16:00 on its day); a training pair reads what its own decision could read, as repo_model.s3c_net.NetSizeTable does. A date of a year no capture shows reads 0 at every instant; a date of a year with a capture reads 1 only from the capture's instant, converted from the archive's UTC stamp to America/New_York. All leads are read, each by the same per-date rule: a calendar public before the decision is as public at lead 5 as at lead 1. Leakage test with one recorded mutation: tests/test_sifma_mbs.py (the rule) and tests/test_s3c_mbs.py (the table and the walk)
candidate.pairs: direct: the indicators are read at the target row (training_pairs = 'direct'); fit_mbs_terms is guarded by one_step_guard with no allow-list entry; the provisional-register row is metadata/provisional/cleared/s3c_mbs_1276.json

frame.windows: the development window (targets up to 2025-12-31, as #1145, #1241 and #1255) and the 2026 development days (targets 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03, the near-blind tier open since GO #151, as #1229, #1252 and #1255), the frames of scripts/s3c_candidate_1255.py, loaded as they are
frame.walk: (s3)'s walk is #1229's and #1255's (every decision day from the start of the panel, refit every 21 decision days, direct pairs); the arm is walked on the same days with the same refit schedule, and (s3) re-forecast inside it must equal the frame's (s3) cell for cell or the run stops

arms.name: sc_s3c_mbs
arms.role: (s3c-mbs), (s3c) with the agency MBS class settlement-day indicators

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp), the probability read off the 23 quantiles as 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between them (spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event strict and on whole basis points (data.exceeds_bp)
primary.comparisons: (s3c-mbs) paired with (s3c) and with (s3), and against B1, B1' and B2
primary.calibration: the 90% band coverage (closed band q05 to q95) of (s3c-mbs) beside (s3c)'s and (s3)'s, pooled, by regime, by lead and on the days the terms are non-zero; means, not tested

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1276, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): the arm is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.splits: pooled; by regime; by pressure-day type of the target day; by lead; by calendar target-day type and target month (as #1255 has them); and the target days on which the changed terms are non-zero (a settlement day of some class, read at lead 1) against the other target days, and each class's settlement days against the other days (a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested). The intervals of a group of target days keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide
scoring.identical_groups: a group in which an arm's score equals the reference's on every day is listed as identical and not tested against it

fitted_effect: the fitted effect of each indicator in bp, by regime: on each (decision day, lead) cell where the indicator is 1, coefficient (of the refit in force) * the scale at the decision's anchor; the count, the mean, the smallest and the largest, by the regime of the target day, for each class (or the pooled indicator); and the coefficient of each refit, summarised by the regime of the refit day (the median, the range and the number of refits in which the indicator is active)
reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c) stays the candidate until she rules on the result.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime, pressure-day-type and settlement-day splits beside it. The settlement days are few in the years the archive shows; the page states the counts.
The page says plainly in which years the indicators can be non-zero under the availability rule, and that in every other year the arm is (s3c) up to the refit of the fit.
The page cites no source for the idea beyond her ruling and compares with no outside figure.
The page ends with marked questions for Eleonora with numbered options and defaults that change no claim.
